steps.name: Sample structure QC
steps.question: Do the 60 case and 60 control whole-blood samples in counts.csv / metadata.csv separate on the major axes of variance, and are there outlier samples or a hidden batch structure before any test runs?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC on raw counts: blind vst, PCA on top-variable genes, sample distance heatmap, per R-0033.

steps.description: Load counts.csv (12000 genes x 120 samples, first column gene symbol) and metadata.csv (120 samples x condition), match sample IDs between the two files and report any mismatches or dropped samples. Build a DESeqDataSet with design ~1 purely for a blind variance-stabilizing transform (this is for visualization only; the DE test itself uses limma-voom, not DESeq2, per the population-cohort caution below). Compute PCA on the 500 most variable vst(blind) genes colored by condition, a sample-to-sample Euclidean distance heatmap, and a library-size (total raw count) boxplot by condition. Flag any sample that is a PCA or library-size outlier, and state explicitly that the data context reports a single batch so no batch correction is planned.
acceptance_criteria: Sample IDs in counts.csv and metadata.csv are matched and any mismatches reported
PCA plot on top 500 variable vst-blind genes, colored by condition, is produced
Sample distance heatmap and library size boxplot are produced
Any outlier or mismatched samples are explicitly named in the output

steps.name: limma-voom DE with effect-size (TREAT) triage and Wilcoxon control
caveats: In a population cohort of this size, DESeq2/edgeR negative-binomial models report many false positives even on permuted labels; limma-voom keeps the false discovery rate closer to nominal but can still exceed it, so the Wilcoxon control result must be reported alongside the primary result, not omitted.
steps.question: Which genes differ between the 60 cases and 60 controls (limma-voom fixed-effects test, FDR<0.05), and which of those also pass a biologically meaningful effect-size threshold (TREAT against |log2FC|>=1), with a per-gene Wilcoxon rank-sum test as a non-parametric robustness check?

grounding.reason: R-0015 overrides the default DESeq2/apeglm path because each arm has 60 (>=50) samples: switched primary test to limma-voom with a Wilcoxon control, and used TREAT (R-0037) instead of apeglm shrinkage (apeglm is DESeq2-specific and not applicable to a limma-voom fit).

steps.description: Filter low-count genes with edgeR::filterByExpr (group = condition, min.count=10, min samples = smallest group size = 60), report genes retained out of 12000. TMM-normalize with edgeR::calcNormFactors. Read the actual condition level strings from metadata.csv, set 'control' as the explicit reference level, and build design ~0+condition with contrast case-control named explicitly. Because each arm holds 60 samples (>=50), negative-binomial count models (DESeq2, edgeR-QLF) are known to over-call on population cohorts even under permuted labels, so the primary test is limma-voom (voom -> lmFit -> eBayes, robust=TRUE) on the TMM-normalized filtered counts, NOT DESeq2/edgeR-QLF. Report the plain FDR<0.05 result table (log2FC, CI, moderated t, p, padj) and, separately, a TREAT/topTreat test against a log2FC threshold of 1 (2-fold) to identify genes whose effect is large enough to matter, not only statistically significant -- report the count of genes significant by padj alone vs. the count also passing the TREAT threshold. As the required orthogonal control for the population-cohort false-positive caution, run a two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test per gene on log2-CPM values (case vs control), BH-adjust, and report the overlap between the limma-voom significant set and the Wilcoxon significant set. Produce the voom mean-variance trend plot, the limma mean-difference (MD) plot, and the p-value histogram of the primary test as fit diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Number of genes retained after filterByExpr is reported out of the 12000 tested
Design uses an explicit reference level (control) and a named contrast (case - control)
Primary DE test is limma-voom, not DESeq2 or edgeR-QLF, with justification stated
Both a plain FDR<0.05 table and a TREAT (|log2FC|>=1) table are reported with counts of genes in each
A per-gene Wilcoxon rank-sum test is run and its overlap with the limma-voom significant set is reported
Voom mean-variance plot, MD plot, and p-value histogram are produced

steps.name: Whole-blood immune cell composition
steps.question: Do the 60 cases and 60 controls differ in immune cell composition, and could that composition shift explain part of the case/control gene expression differences seen in whole blood?

grounding.reason: Whole-blood composition context for a bulk DE result: MCP-counter/quanTIseq/EPIC on linear-scale CPM, reported as a covariate/confound for the DE genes, not a replacement for the design (R-0132).

steps.description: Convert the raw gene-level counts to CPM (linear scale). Note that only gene-level counts are available, not transcript-level quantifications with gene lengths, so exact TPM cannot be computed; CPM is used as the linear-scale input, which is standard when lengths are unavailable. Compute MCP-counter scores (log2-CPM input) for immune/stromal populations and quanTIseq and EPIC absolute fractions (linear-CPM input) via the immunedeconv interface. Test each cell-type score/fraction between case and control with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test, BH-adjusted across the tested cell types. Report which populations differ and flag any overlap between those populations' canonical marker genes (e.g., neutrophil, T-cell, B-cell, monocyte markers) and the genes found differentially expressed in T1S2, to signal which DE genes may reflect composition change rather than cell-intrinsic regulation.
acceptance_criteria: CPM conversion is used for deconvolution input, and the lack of transcript-level lengths (no true TPM) is stated explicitly
MCP-counter, quanTIseq and EPIC scores/fractions are computed for all 120 samples
Each cell type is tested case vs control with BH-adjusted Wilcoxon p-values
Overlap between differing cell-type marker genes and the T1S2 DE gene list is reported

steps.name: Pathway and hallmark enrichment on the case vs control contrast
steps.question: Which coordinated gene sets (Hallmark, Reactome, WikiPathways) are enriched in the case vs control contrast, using the full ranked gene list rather than only the FDR-significant genes?

grounding.reason: Population-scale cohort (>=50/group): enrichment runs on the limma-voom fit with camera plus fgsea on the moderated t-statistic (R-0088), Hallmark then Reactome/WikiPathways as follow-up collections (R-0098, R-0165), ranking metric stated per disputed rule R-0108.

steps.description: Rank all genes tested in T1S2 (post-filter) by the limma-voom moderated t-statistic of the case-control contrast (chosen as the ranking metric because it is the same statistic driving the DE call and scales the effect by its uncertainty; state this choice explicitly since the ranking metric is a disputed choice in the literature). Run camera (limma) directly on the voom fit as the primary competitive gene set test, with inter-gene correlation estimated from the data, against the MSigDB human Hallmark gene sets (50 sets). Run fgsea preranked on the same ranked list against Hallmark, then as follow-up collections against the Reactome human pathway gene sets and the WikiPathways human collection staged in the reference store -- gene matching is by symbol directly since the count matrix is gene-symbol indexed and all three collections are HGNC-symbol GMTs, so no Entrez ID mapping is needed. Apply a gene set size window of 15-500 genes (after intersecting with the tested genes) to every collection, BH-adjust within each collection separately (do not merge collections), and state each collection's release/version. Report the number of genes significant at padj<0.05 in T1S2; if fewer than ~50, state explicitly that no over-representation analysis is run and that the ranked methods (camera, fgsea) are the sole enrichment result. Collapse redundant significant sets and list the leading-edge genes for each reported significant set.
acceptance_criteria: Ranking metric (moderated t-statistic) is stated explicitly as the chosen side of the disputed ranking-metric rule
camera is run on the voom fit against Hallmark; fgsea preranked is run against Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways human collections separately
Each collection's version/release is stated in the output
Gene set size window of 15-500 is applied and stated
No over-representation test is run unless >=50 genes are FDR-significant in T1S2; this condition is checked and reported
Leading-edge genes are reported for each significant gene set

steps.name: Consolidated report: significance, effect size, composition context, and pathways
steps.question: What is the full, decision-ready answer to which genes differ between cases and controls, which differences are large enough to matter biologically (not just statistically significant), and how much of the signal is confounded by whole-blood cell composition or method choice?

grounding.reason: Report consolidates effect size beside p-value (R-0089), fit diagnostics (R-0087), enrichment provenance and method-disagreement caution (R-0051, R-0055), leading-edge genes (R-0105), and a full reproducibility record (R-0086).

steps.description: Consolidate T1S1 QC diagnostics, T1S2 DE results (plain FDR<0.05 table and TREAT effect-size table, Wilcoxon overlap, voom/MD/p-value-histogram diagnostics), T2S1 immune composition results and any marker-gene overlap with the DE list, and T2S2 enrichment results (camera + fgsea across Hallmark/Reactome/WikiPathways with leading-edge genes). Report gene tables with unshrunken log2FC, its standard error, and moderated t/p/padj columns; sort the significant gene table by effect size, not by p-value alone, and state the number of genes tested, the number significant by padj<0.05, and the number also passing the TREAT |log2FC|>=1 threshold. State explicitly that the DE test used limma-voom rather than DESeq2/edgeR because each arm has 60 samples, and give the Wilcoxon-test overlap as the required robustness caveat. State that only gene-level (not transcript-level) salmon counts were available, so no tximport gene-length offset could be applied. State each enrichment collection's version and that enrichment methods can disagree (report camera vs fgsea overlap/disagreement). Attach a full reproducibility record: package versions, random seeds used, and gene-set collection versions.
acceptance_criteria: Report states n tested, n significant (padj<0.05), and n passing the TREAT effect-size threshold, with the significant table sorted by effect size
Report explicitly states and justifies the limma-voom (not DESeq2/edgeR) choice and reports the Wilcoxon-test overlap as a caveat
Report states the whole-blood immune composition context and flags any DE genes overlapping cell-type markers
Report states each enrichment collection's version, the ranking metric used, and reports overlap/disagreement between camera and fgsea
Report includes a reproducibility record: package versions, seeds, and collection versions

plan.title: Whole-blood case vs control DE with effect-size triage
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12000 x 120 raw gene-level (salmon-derived, gene-symbol-indexed) counts from a single-batch, unpaired 60-case vs 60-control whole-blood cohort. At 60 samples per arm, negative-binomial count models (DESeq2/edgeR-QLF) are known to inflate false positives on population cohorts because sample-to-sample variance no longer follows the NB assumption, so the primary DE test is limma-voom with a fixed-effects linear model, cross-checked with a per-gene Wilcoxon rank-sum test as a non-parametric control. Because the question explicitly separates 'significant' from 'large enough to matter', the DE step reports both a plain FDR<0.05 test and a TREAT test against an explicit log2FC threshold, and the report ranks and sorts genes by effect size, not p-value alone. Because the tissue is whole blood, a large share of any case/control transcriptional difference can be driven by immune cell composition shifts rather than cell-intrinsic regulation, so an immune deconvolution step runs in parallel to give that context before the gene table is over-interpreted. Enrichment runs on the full ranked gene list (camera on the voom fit, plus fgsea preranked on the moderated t-statistic) against Hallmark, Reactome and WikiPathways human collections staged in the reference store, using symbol-based matching since the count matrix is already gene-symbol indexed. A final report step consolidates QC diagnostics, the significance-vs-effect-size gene tables, the immune-composition confound, and the enrichment results with full reproducibility metadata.
